parameters.query:
-- Sweeper (every 2 min): batches whose doorbell was missed, or whose matcher died mid-run.
-- The 1-minute grace period gives the webhook path first chance, so the two rarely collide
-- (and when they do, the claim below lets only one win).
SELECT id::text AS batch_id
FROM ingest_batches
WHERE (status = 'LOADED' AND updated_at < now() - interval '1 minute')
   OR (status = 'MATCHING' AND lease_until < now())
ORDER BY created_at
LIMIT 1;  -- one batch per tick keeps each execution single-batch; ticks are 2 min apart

-- Compare-and-set claim with a 15-minute lease. Zero rows back = someone else owns it → stop.
-- $1 = batch_id
WITH claimed AS (
  UPDATE ingest_batches
     SET status = 'MATCHING', lease_until = now() + interval '15 minutes', updated_at = now()
   WHERE id = $1::uuid
     AND (status = 'LOADED' OR (status = 'MATCHING' AND lease_until < now()))
  RETURNING id
), ev AS (
  INSERT INTO pipeline_events (batch_id, stage, status) SELECT id, 'match', 'started' FROM claimed
)
SELECT id::text AS batch_id FROM claimed;

-- The entire active catalogue as ONE row holding a JSON array: n8n's cost is per item,
-- so a list travels as one item, not hundreds.
SELECT coalesce(json_agg(p ORDER BY p.id), '[]'::json) AS products
FROM (
  SELECT id, lender_name, product_name, source_url, interest_rate_min, interest_rate_max,
         min_monthly_income, min_credit_score, accepts_ntc, min_age, max_age,
         employment_types::text[] AS employment_types, max_loan_amount, soft_rules, criteria_hash
  FROM loan_products
  WHERE is_active
) p;

-- Treasure Hunt stage 1: "fetch the newly added users", already compressed into classes.
-- width_bucket maps each value to the interval between product thresholds (coordinate
-- compression); users in the same intervals on every attribute are identical to every product.
-- Credit NULL (new-to-credit) gets bucket 0. Returns one row: {classes:[...], users:n}.
-- $1 batch_id, $2 income cuts, $3 credit cuts, $4 age cuts (Postgres array literals of numbers)
SELECT coalesce(json_agg(c), '[]'::json) AS classes, coalesce(sum(c.n), 0)::int AS users
FROM (
  SELECT width_bucket(monthly_income, $2::numeric[])                  AS ib,
         coalesce(width_bucket(credit_score, $3::numeric[]), 0)       AS cb,
         width_bucket(age, $4::numeric[])                             AS ab,
         employment_status::text                                      AS emp,
         count(*)::int                                                AS n
  FROM users
  WHERE last_batch_id = $1::uuid
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
) c;

-- Stage 3 cache lookup. $1 = JSON array of cache keys. Returns one row: {judgments: {key: verdict}}.
SELECT coalesce(json_object_agg(cache_key, verdict), '{}'::json) AS judgments
FROM llm_judgments
WHERE cache_key IN (SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text($1::jsonb));

-- $1 = JSON array of {cache_key, product_id, verdict, rationale, model}
INSERT INTO llm_judgments (cache_key, product_id, verdict, rationale, model)
SELECT cache_key, product_id, verdict, rationale, model
FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb)
     AS j(cache_key text, product_id bigint, verdict text, rationale text, model text)
WHERE verdict IN ('PASS', 'FAIL', 'UNKNOWN')
ON CONFLICT (cache_key) DO NOTHING
RETURNING cache_key;

-- One atomic statement: expand class results back to users, upsert `matches`, drop matches the
-- batch's users no longer qualify for, record the funnel, and mark the batch MATCHED.
-- n8n ships ~hundreds of class rows; Postgres expands them to tens of thousands of pairs
-- (set-based, one round trip) instead of n8n sending one INSERT per pair.
-- Existing pairs keep first_matched_at and notified_at, so nobody is emailed twice for the same offer.
-- $1 batch_id, $2 class rows JSON, $3/$4/$5 income/credit/age cuts, $6 funnel JSON
WITH cls AS (
  SELECT * FROM jsonb_to_recordset($2::jsonb) AS c(
    ib int, cb int, ab int, emp text, product_id bigint, status text, score real,
    unverified jsonb, decided_by text)
), batch_users AS (
  SELECT user_id,
         width_bucket(monthly_income, $3::numeric[])            AS ib,
         coalesce(width_bucket(credit_score, $4::numeric[]), 0) AS cb,
         width_bucket(age, $5::numeric[])                       AS ab,
         employment_status::text                                AS emp
  FROM users WHERE last_batch_id = $1::uuid
), fresh AS (
  SELECT u.user_id, c.product_id, c.status, c.score, c.unverified, c.decided_by
  FROM batch_users u JOIN cls c USING (ib, cb, ab, emp)
), removed AS (
  DELETE FROM matches m USING batch_users u
  WHERE m.user_id = u.user_id
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fresh f WHERE f.user_id = m.user_id AND f.product_id = m.product_id)
  RETURNING 1
), upserted AS (
  INSERT INTO matches (user_id, product_id, status, score, unverified, decided_by, batch_id)
  SELECT user_id, product_id, status, score, unverified, decided_by, $1::uuid FROM fresh
  ON CONFLICT (user_id, product_id) DO UPDATE
     SET status = EXCLUDED.status, score = EXCLUDED.score, unverified = EXCLUDED.unverified,
         decided_by = EXCLUDED.decided_by, batch_id = EXCLUDED.batch_id
  RETURNING (xmax = 0) AS is_new
), counts AS (
  SELECT count(*) AS matches, count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_new) AS new_matches,
         (SELECT count(*) FROM removed) AS removed
  FROM upserted
), done AS (
  UPDATE ingest_batches SET status = 'MATCHED', lease_until = NULL, updated_at = now()
  WHERE id = $1::uuid AND status = 'MATCHING'
  RETURNING id
), ev AS (
  INSERT INTO pipeline_events (batch_id, stage, status, detail)
  SELECT $1::uuid, 'match', 'completed',
         $6::jsonb || jsonb_build_object('stored_matches', matches, 'new_matches', new_matches, 'removed', removed)
  FROM counts
)
SELECT $1 AS batch_id, matches, new_matches, removed, (SELECT count(*) FROM done) AS transitioned FROM counts;
